text:
Arjun: Heads-up — the nightly telemetry backfill we kicked off is bumping into our routing quotas for priority lanes. Some tenants are getting preempted and the console cost estimate is way off :grimacing:
Maya: Ugh. Is the estimate mismatch the UI using sampled cost while the job uses full-per-token accounting? :eyes:
Arjun: Yup. Console shows a rough ‘expected cost’ from the dry-run path that ignores KV-cache hit improvements and model quantization we enable server-side. The actual run billed ~2.4x the UI estimate for a small subset last night.
Liz: For Dedicated customers we need deterministic preflight checks. If the dry-run and live runs diverge that much we should gate by an API-level preflight that returns a high/low bound and an explicit "budget_ok" flag.
Sam: Agree on API preflight. Proposal: add /v1/backfills/preflight that accepts routing_hint and quant_profile, returns {cost_est_low, cost_est_high, budget_ok, token_breakdown}. Minimal change and backwards compatible. Example call:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/backfills/preflight \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -d '{"tenant_id":"t-123","query":"agg_hours","window":"2026-03-01..2026-03-02","routing_hint":"priority_lane", "quant_profile":"q3"}'
```
Maya: +1. Also can we show both the dry-run (console) estimate and the API preflight bounds in the UI? Right now the console hides variance which causes ops to under-commit quota.
Henry: ops-bot: scheduled job 2026-03-01-backfill-42 started (run_id r-77f). Current progress: 18% tokens processed. No errors.
Arjun: ops-bot yay, but we need the UI to surface the preflight bound as a required confirmation step for tenant admins.
Liz: If we add a budget_ok boolean, how do we handle shared pools where a tenant's budget check passes but queue-level quotas still throttle? We need a pre-reserve API to atomically claim a slot or nonce.
Sam: We could add a two-phase lease: preflight->reserve (short TTL) -> commit. Reserve returns lease_id and expected_token_charge. If quota allocation fails at reserve, the preflight still helped but reserve fails safely.
Maya: UX question — how do we present uncertain estimates to users without scaring them? Suggest showing low/median/high + confidence band and a "expected impact on monthly invoice" slider that maps to their billing granularity.
Arjun: Good. Also ask infra: can the serving runtime expose an enum for the effective optimizations used in the run so the preflight can simulate identical runtime conditions? Right now preflight assumes optimistic cache hits.
Liz: Runtime fingerprinting sounds right: include fields like {kernel_variant, kv_cache_mode, quant_profile} in the preflight response so preflight and live runs are comparable.
Sam: Implementation note: keep preflight fast by sampling traces and extrapolating. We should warn users when sampling variance > 20%.
ops-bot: reminder: please annotate "sensitive tenants" in the backfill job metadata to enforce stricter preflight/reserve checks.
Maya: I'll mock up the console changes — side-by-side preflight bounds + live estimate + "reserve" CTA. Also add a toggle for "enforce reserve for shared pools".
Arjun: Can someone pair with Sam to draft the API schema and wireframe the modal? I'll take the runtime fingerprinting piece with Liz.
Sam: I can do API draft tomorrow morning. Ping me after your mock, Maya.
Liz: I'll sketch the reserve flow and quota race conditions. Will post a tiny sequence diagram.
Arjun: Thanks all. If we can ship preflight+reserve and show confidence bands in the console before next large backfill, we should avoid surprises. :thumbsup:
Maya: Filed a console spike ticket and added initial mock to the design board.
Henry: ops-bot: noted. Next nightly backfill will include the "sensitive tenants" flag where present.
Sam: Quick follow-up — do we want the preflight endpoint to accept an explicit sampling_seed so engineers can reproduce estimates?
Maya: Yes, add sampling_seed and a human-readable reason field so audit logs show why a reserve was taken.
Arjun: Perfect. We'll iterate on the schema in the ticket. End of thread.
